Let me analyze this task. I need to estimate software development effort for a set of user stories related to Spring XD (based on the context - Hadoop, jdbchdfs batch jobs, modules, DSL sessions, XD-on-Lattice/Diego, module docs, shell processor with Python).

The user stories:
- U1: Migrate wiki to project repo so it can be tagged with code and versioned
- U2: Add Hadoop namenode specifics in config file for automatic configuration in DSL sessions
- U3: jdbchdfs batch job passthrough (without chunk processing) to avoid batch read/write overhead
- U4: Decouple execution context from job launch lifecycle (upgrade Spring Batch, refactor XD-2486 workaround)
- U5: Custom job module using Java Config support (fix deployment/launch error)
- U6: XD-on-Lattice/Diego PoC with pluggable SPI design (Receptor API as one implementation)
- U7: Update module docs to include shortDescription
- U8: Host/read Python script from HDFS for shell processor in XD on CF

Let me build a WBS:

Project-level activities:
1. Requirements analysis & design
2. Per user story implementation
3. Integration & testing
4. Documentation
5. Build/release management

Let me think about effort estimates per story. I'll estimate in work-hours as a single developer.

U1: Wiki migration to repo (e.g., convert GitHub wiki to asciidoc/markdown in repo, set up build integration). Effort: ~16-24 hours. Let's say 24h including conversion, link fixes, verification.

U2: Hadoop namenode config in config file (e.g., hadoop.properties / servers.yml, XD shell reading fs.defaultFS at startup). Design + implementation + tests: ~24-32h. Say 32h.

U3: jdbchdfs passthrough job (no chunk processing) - new job module variant, tasklet-based implementation, tests: ~40h.

U4: Decouple execution context from job launch lifecycle - depends on Spring Batch upgrade. Upgrade XD to new Spring Batch release, refactor XD-2486 workaround, regression testing: ~40-56h. Say 48h.

U5: Custom job module with Java Config - fix classloading/module deployment to support Java Config based jobs, reproduce error, fix, tests, docs: ~40h.

U6: XD-on-Lattice/Diego PoC with pluggable SPI design - this is a larger design + PoC effort: ~80-120h. Say 100h.

U7: Update module docs with shortDescription - metadata addition across many modules, doc updates: ~24h.

U8: Python script hosting/read from HDFS for shell processor - HDFS resource support in shell processor, script retrieval, feedback: ~40h.

Plus cross-cutting:
- Overall requirements/architecture alignment: 16h
- Integration testing & CI: 24h
- Code review/rework: maybe included per story
- Documentation & release notes: 16h

Let me structure the WBS more formally:

1. Project setup & requirements analysis (16h)
2. U1 - Wiki migration (24h)
3. U2 - Hadoop namenode configuration (32h)
4. U3 - jdbchdfs passthrough job (40h)
5. U4 - Execution context decoupling / Spring Batch upgrade (48h)
6. U5 - Java Config custom job module support (40h)
7. U6 - Pluggable SPI design + XD-on-Lattice/Diego PoC (100h)
8. U7 - Module docs shortDescription (24h)
9. U8 - Python script from HDFS in shell processor (40h)
10. Integration & system testing (24h)
11. Documentation & release notes (16h)

Total: 16+24+32+40+48+40+100+24+40+24+16 = 404h

Total = 404 work-hours.

Actually the spec intro describes Spring Framework generally. XD-on-Lattice/Diego PoC places it ~2015, so Spring XD 1.1/1.2, Spring Batch 3.x, Java 8. technical_and_design_decisions: Target codebase is Spring XD 1.x (Java 8, Gradle multi-module build, Spring Batch 3.x, Spring Integration 4.x); the Spring Framework 6 / Java 17 note in the specification is treated as background context only, not as a migration target.

U1: Migrate the GitHub wiki to AsciiDoc sources stored under docs/ in the main project repository, built with the Asciidoctor Gradle plugin, so documentation is versioned and tagged together with the code; wiki pages are frozen with a redirect notice.

U2: Externalize the Hadoop namenode (fs.defaultFS / spring.hadoop.fsUri) into config/servers.yml and hadoop.properties; the XD shell and admin server auto-configure the Hadoop FileSystem at session startup so no per-session URI is required.

U3: Implement the jdbchdfs passthrough as a new tasklet-based (non-chunk-oriented) job module variant that streams JdbcTemplate query results directly to an HDFS writer, exposed via module options; the existing chunk-based module remains unchanged.

U4: Upgrade the Spring Batch dependency to the released version containing the execution-context/job-lifecycle fix, remove the XD-2486 serialization workaround and its configuration switches, and add regression tests covering distributed job launch and restart.

U5: Extend the module launcher/classloading so job modules can be defined with Java Config: detect @Configuration/@EnableBatchProcessing classes in the uploaded module jar and bootstrap them with an AnnotationConfigApplicationContext; reproduce and fix the reported 'job doesn't exist' deployment error.

U6: Define a pluggable runtime SPI (ModuleDeployer/ContainerProvider-style interface) decoupling XD's runtime from any specific platform; implement the Lattice/Diego support as one SPI provider using the Receptor API, delivered as a proof of concept with a design document.

U7: Add a shortDescription field to module metadata (module properties / ModuleDescriptor), surface it in module listing and documentation generation, and update all existing module AsciiDoc documents to include it.

U8: Extend the shell processor to resolve hdfs:// script URIs through the Hadoop FileSystem API, stream the Python script to a local temporary file before process execution, and pipe stdout/stderr back into XD messages.
assumptions: Effort is estimated for a single experienced developer already familiar with the Spring XD codebase; only work effort is estimated, not elapsed calendar duration.

Each per-story activity estimate includes detailed design, implementation, unit tests, and code-review rework; cross-cutting integration/system testing and release documentation are estimated as separate activities.

For U4, the required fix is already available in a released Spring Batch version; no changes to Spring Batch source code itself are needed, only the dependency upgrade and removal of the XD-2486 workaround.
For U6, the deliverable is a design document plus a working proof of concept, not production-hardened code.
For U7, approximately 50 existing module documents and the shared module metadata/plugin code are in scope.
CI/build infrastructure (Gradle CI jobs) already exists; only configuration updates are required.
A single-node Hadoop test cluster with HDFS access is available for development and testing of U2, U3, and U8.
No clarifying questions were asked; all specification gaps are resolved through the recorded assumptions.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, confirm scope and acceptance criteria, align on the technical approach for each story (configuration model, module system changes, SPI design outline), and set up the development environment and feature branches.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Migrate wiki to project repository
activities.activity_description: Convert existing wiki pages to AsciiDoc sources under docs/ in the main repo, integrate the Asciidoctor Gradle plugin into the build, fix internal links and images, verify rendering, and freeze the old wiki with redirect notices so docs are tagged and versioned with the code.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Hadoop namenode configuration file support
activities.activity_description: Add namenode settings (fs.defaultFS / spring.hadoop.fsUri) to config/servers.yml and hadoop.properties, implement auto-configuration of the Hadoop FileSystem at XD shell/admin session startup, and add unit and integration tests covering default and overridden configurations.

Implement a tasklet-based, non-chunk jdbchdfs job module variant that streams JDBC results directly to HDFS without batch read/write chunk overhead, expose the relevant module options, and provide unit and integration tests plus a sample job definition.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Decouple execution context from job launch lifecycle
activities.activity_description: Upgrade the Spring Batch dependency to the release containing the execution-context fix, refactor and remove the XD-2486 workaround and its configuration switches, resolve resulting classloading/serialization issues, and add regression tests for distributed job launch, restart, and partitioning scenarios.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Java Config support for custom job modules
activities.activity_description: Reproduce the reported deployment error for a Java Config-based custom job module, extend module classloading/launching to detect @Configuration/@EnableBatchProcessing classes and bootstrap them via an AnnotationConfigApplicationContext, fix the job registration issue, and add tests plus a reference sample module.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Pluggable runtime SPI design and XD-on-Lattice/Diego PoC
activities.activity_description: Produce the SPI design document, define and refactor a pluggable ModuleDeployer/ContainerProvider-style SPI in the XD runtime, implement a Lattice/Diego provider based on the Receptor API, and validate the PoC by deploying and launching stream/job modules on a Diego/Lattice environment.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Add shortDescription to module documentation and metadata
activities.activity_description: Extend module metadata (module properties / ModuleDescriptor) with a shortDescription field, surface it in module listings and doc generation, and update all existing module AsciiDoc documents and the module plugin tests accordingly.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Host and read Python scripts from HDFS in shell processor
activities.activity_description: Extend the shell processor to resolve hdfs:// script URIs via the Hadoop FileSystem API, stream the Python script to a local temp file before execution, capture stdout/stderr back into XD messages, and test end-to-end in the XD-on-CF environment.

Run full integration and system test suites across all delivered stories (distributed transport, Hadoop integration, module deployment, batch job lifecycle), investigate and fix defects found, and perform regression validation of the Spring Batch upgrade.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, release notes, and build/CI updates
activities.activity_description: Update user and reference documentation for the new features (config file settings, passthrough job, Java Config modules, shortDescription, HDFS scripts, SPI), write release notes and migration guidance for the Batch upgrade, and adjust Gradle/CI jobs for the docs build and new modules.
